_note: The AWS worker pool. `aws.default.json` (this file, tracked) ships the shape, so a clone knows what a pool needs; your values live in `.bm/aws.json`, which git ignores — `bm-inductor aws init` copies this there and you fill in the account fields. Same split as the voice catalogue: `voices.default.json` ships, `.bm/voices.json` is yours. No credentials belong in either file; they come from the standard AWS chain (AWS_PROFILE, SSO, or an instance role).
_note_region: Where the boxes run. A pool lives in one region: keypairs and AMIs are region-scoped, which is why `keypairs` is a map rather than a name.
_note_instance_type: CPU-bound: the TTS path is a hand-written SIMD matvec and there is no GPU code. 2 vCPU is the floor (668 MB of models plus a working set); 4 stops render queueing behind itself.
_note_disk_gb: Root volume. Models 668 MB + the profile 57 MB + the segments a chapter accumulates.
_note_subnet_id: A private subnet. The workers dial out, so nothing here needs a public address.
_note_security_group_id: Egress matters (S3, and the inductor); ingress only has to allow ssh from wherever you run this.
_note_iam_instance_profile: The instance profile NAME (not an ARN). This is what lets a box pull its own asset plane from S3 instead of receiving a 668 MB upload from your connection.
_note_ssh_user: `ubuntu` on the stock Ubuntu AMIs, `ec2-user` on Amazon Linux.
_note_keypairs: region -> the EC2 keypair NAME in that region. Create it with `aws ec2 create-key-pair` and keep the private half at `.bm/aws/<region>.pem` (0600) — `.bm/` is already gitignored, so the material never enters the tree.
_note_images: region -> the AMI ID. Explicit on purpose: the image decides what actually runs on your account, so it should be a decision you made and can see, not a 'latest' pointer that moves under you. Resolve the current Ubuntu LTS with:  aws ssm get-parameter --name /aws/service/canonical/ubuntu/server/24.04/stable/current/amd64/hvm/ebs-gp3/ami-id --region <region> --query Parameter.Value --output text    It must match ssh_user above (ubuntu on Ubuntu, ec2-user on Amazon Linux).
_note_bucket: Where the profile bundles are published, named by their manifest hash. Empty is a working configuration: every box then receives the assets by rsync from your machine, which is fine on a LAN and 668 MB per box from home.
_note_spot: Spot is a good fit: render and merge are both idempotent and the lease reaper requeues an interrupted task, so a reclaimed box costs a retry rather than a lost chapter.
_note_max_workers: Hard cap on concurrently registered cloud boxes. A launch that would exceed it is refused rather than left to the caller's arithmetic.
_note_ttl_hours: Default lifetime. A box that outlives its work is the whole cost of a cloud pool.
_note_tag_key: Every box this tool starts carries this tag, so `ls` and `down` can never touch anything else in the account. Its value is the profile hash the box was launched for.
